newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Rough Canberra rally for Bourne.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Rough Canberra rally for Bourne.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Nov 14 - Pukekohe mechanic Kevin Sanderson is performing a last minute dash to get parts to Possum Bourne's Subaru WRX for this weekend's Canberra rally, NZPA reports.
The three-day event which starts on Friday is the final round of the Australian championship which Bourne and Hamilton co-driver Craig Vincent won at Coffs Harbour last month.
Sanderson, one of Bourne's team, is taking special rough road suspension units to Sydney this morning to fit to the Subaru in time for the Friday lunchtime start.
"The roads are as rough as guts," Bourne said.
"We've decided to raise the Impreza's suspension to something like they use on the Acropolis world championship event."
The Acropolis is considered to be the roughest round of the world series.
"We haven't encountered anything like this on any other rounds of the Aussie series," Bourne said.
Even home-town hero Neal Bates, who has been seeded second behind Bourne, has found some unprintable adjectives to describe the route he won over 12 months ago.
Victory over the 330kms of special stages may come down to who has the least problems during the stages, according to Bourne.
"The roads are going to be hard on any car. A good consistent drive and staying out of trouble might pay the best dividends."
Bourne will be attempting to win his sixth event of the series and finish the championship with a perfect points score.
